name: OTPEntry
description:
OTP Challenge

Enter this code: <the 6-digit code shown on the page; it changes on every load>
notes: routes.ts: "Enter a 6-digit one-time password with auto-focusing inputs" (base variant, medium). The page shows "Enter this code: NNNNNN" (random on every load, so the description uses a placeholder) above six unlabeled single-character textboxes (maxLength=1). Typing a digit moves focus to the next box, so key-by-key typing into the first box works (Playwright keyboard.type / pressSequentially, agent-browser keyboard type, playwright-cli type after clicking box 1); filling each box separately also works. A one-shot fill() of the whole code into box 1 keeps only the first digit (verified 5/5: e.g. "5|||||") and silently does nothing else. A complete wrong code shows "Incorrect code. Please try again." (no lockout); the boxes are then full and must be overwritten or the page reloaded (new code). Success: "Success! The password is: OTP_MASTER_2024". Caveat (from source): pasting the code (paste event) also reveals the password, but that code path never records a completion, so a paste-based solve fails the server completion check.

name: TextMirrorHard
description:
Text Mirror Challenge (Hard)

Copy the text exactly as shown on the left into the text area on the right. Every single character, including whitespace and line breaks, matters!
notes: routes.ts: "Perfectly copy the longer, more complex text with code and special characters." (HARD variant, chosen over base text-mirror because it stresses text fidelity much more: base trims and has no indentation). The original is a 558-character JavaScript snippet in a whitespace-pre-wrap div: 19 LF newlines, 2/4-space indentation, one blank line, and the characters ` $ { } \\ " ' < > |. Submit checks an exact string match (no trim), including the final newline after "*/". innerText/textContent of the div preserve all of it (innerText ends with "*/\n"), but accessibility snapshots (Playwright aria and AI snapshots, i.e. what Playwright MCP and playwright-cli snapshot return) collapse all whitespace to single spaces (verified), so copying from a snapshot fails. The snippet contains the literal two-character sequences \n and \t (backslash + letter), not real tabs. Enter it in the textarea "Type the text here..." and click Submit; CLI tools must get the text through shell quoting (backticks, $, backslashes, both quote types, newlines). A mismatch silently does nothing. Success: "🎉 Congratulations! ... The secret password is: SuperComplexTextMaster2024".

name: ScrollHorizontal
description:
Scroll to the Right

Keep scrolling horizontally to reveal the secret password!
notes: routes.ts: "Scroll right to find the password" (no variant field, i.e. the default; the Hard variant only doubles the boxes). 50 boxes (300px wide, 80vh tall, text "Keep scrolling! N boxes to go...") sit in a horizontally scrolling div (overflow-x:auto) below a fixed header. The window does not scroll sideways, and the strip is not focusable: End/PageDown, vertical wheel, window scrolling, and arrow keys after clicking the strip do nothing (verified). Works: horizontal wheel/trackpad over the strip (verified: 13 wheel events of deltaX 1200 at 1280px width), or scrolling the last box into view (verified: Playwright hover on "Keep scrolling! 1 boxes to go..."). When at least 10% of the last box is in view (IntersectionObserver) a green box is appended: "Keep scrolling! You made it! Password: SIDEWAYSCROLL2024"; it is removed again if the last box leaves the viewport (possible only in a very narrow window).
mechanic: horizontal scroll inside an overflow container

name: PopupChaos
description:
Popup Chaos

Close all the popup windows to reveal the secret password!
notes: routes.ts: "Close the annoying popup windows to reveal the secret password" (no variant field, i.e. the default). Five 400px-wide position:fixed popups at random positions around the centre overlap each other (z-order = DOM order, last on top). Each has a title bar (drag handle), a close button "✕", and a call-to-action button with a random label ("Learn More", "Install Now", "Close all popups", ...); the CTAs do nothing. All five close buttons have the same accessible name "✕". In 9 recorded loads at 1280x900, 1 to 4 of the five ✕ buttons were covered by another popup at the start (elementFromPoint at the button centre); a real pointer click on a covered ✕ is intercepted (Playwright click refuses: "intercepts pointer events"; a coordinate click hits the popup on top). Closing from the last ✕ in DOM order (the topmost) always works; dragging popups aside by the title bar also works. Popup placement depends on the window size (x <= innerWidth-400, y <= innerHeight-300) and a low popup can be cut off at the bottom (fixed, cannot scroll into view). Success: the centre panel shows "Secret Password" / "PopupSlayer2024" and a toast "Congratulations! You've defeated the popup invasion! The password is: PopupSlayer2024".

name: ButtonHold
description:
Button Hold Challenge

Hold the button down for three seconds!
notes: routes.ts: "Hold the button for exactly 3 seconds" (base variant). The large round button has no text (role button, no name). mousedown starts a timer shown as "0.0s" counting up; mouseup or mouseleave before 3 s resets it to 0.0s (a normal click does nothing). At 3.0 s the page completes by itself while the button is still held; holding longer is fine (no upper limit despite the route text), so agent turn latency is not an issue. Needs a separate mouse-down with the pointer kept over the button: Playwright mouse.down(), playwright-cli mousemove + mousedown, agent-browser mouse move + mouse down; Playwright MCP has browser_mouse_down only with --caps=vision (bench.py starts it without caps), otherwise via browser_evaluate/run_code. A JS-dispatched mousedown event also works (verified). Success: "Congratulations! 🎉 The secret password is: HOLD_STEADY_2024" plus canvas-confetti (local, no network).

name: ClickPixel
description:
Pixel Perfect Challenge

Click anywhere within the 5x5 black square target to complete the challenge.
notes: routes.ts: "Click the single target pixel on the screen." (base variant). A full-viewport board (starts at viewport 0,0) with a 5x5 px black square at a random position at least 100 px from every edge, and the text "Target position: (x, y)" in board coordinates. The square has no text or role and does not appear in accessibility snapshots, so it has no ref: it needs a coordinate click inside x..x+5, y..y+5 (or a CSS-selector / JS click; a JS-dispatched click with clientX/clientY works, verified). Every click re-renders the page and moves the target to a new random position; after a miss the page shows "Last click: (...) - Distance: (...)" and new target coordinates, so the agent must re-read them (a click on the old coordinates fails). Success: "Congratulations! You found the target!" / "Password: PIXEL_PERFECT_2024" in the instruction card.
mechanic: coordinate click on a target with no DOM/a11y handle

name: SliderSymphony
description:
Slider Symphony

Align the colored boxes with their dashed outlines by adjusting the sliders.

The boxes need to be very close to their targets to count as aligned!
notes: routes.ts: "Align the boxes by mastering the vertical sliders!" (base variant, medium; Hard has 6 sliders and a 5 px tolerance, which mostly stresses visual precision, not the tool). Four native <input type=range> (0-100, start 50) drawn vertically (writing-mode vertical-lr, rotated 180°) and exposed only as `slider "50"`. Slider i moves blue box i (top = 10 + 2.4 x value px); the four dashed target outlines sit at random heights and are plain divs that do not appear in accessibility snapshots, so the agent needs a screenshot (or DOM geometry/styles) to see where each box must go. Completes as soon as every box is within 10 px (about 4 slider steps) of its outline. Input quirks (verified): ArrowRight/ArrowLeft = +1/-1 but ArrowUp = -1 on these rotated sliders; dragging the thumb up increases the value, which moves the box down; clicking near the bottom of the track sets 0 (box at the top); Playwright fill() on the range input works (React onChange fires). Success: "Congratulations! You've aligned all the boxes!" / "Password: SMOOTHSLIDER42". The app re-sends the completion event several times per solve (harmless).
mechanic: vertical range sliders aligned to visual-only targets

name: PrintReveal
description:
Print to Reveal

First, print this page or save it as PDF to find the initial password.

Try using your browser's print function (Ctrl/Cmd + P) or "Save as PDF" option.

Then, enter that password below to reveal the final password.

Hint: The initial password is hidden in this page, but you won't see it on screen!
notes: routes.ts: "Print this page to PDF to reveal the hidden password" (only variant). The page adds a print-only stylesheet: in print media the instructions and form are hidden and a block "First Step Complete! ... enter this password: PRINT_2_PDF_8X11 ..." is shown. That intermediate code is in the DOM from the start (display:none: not in innerText, screenshots or accessibility snapshots) and is NOT the task password. Type it into "Enter the password from the PDF..." and click "Verify Password" (screen media) to get "Congratulations! The final password is: PR1NT_V3R1F13D_2024"; a wrong code shows "Incorrect password. Please check the PDF and try again.". Routes in: save as PDF (Playwright page.pdf, playwright-cli pdf, agent-browser pdf; Playwright MCP browser_pdf_save only with --caps=pdf) and read the PDF (pdftotext is at /opt/homebrew/bin/pdftotext; the PDF wraps "enter this / password:" across lines); or emulate print media (e.g. Playwright MCP browser_emulate_media) and read the snapshot, then switch back to screen media to use the form; or read the hidden block from the DOM with JS. Typing PRINT_2_PDF_8X11 is the intended play, so it is not a leak marker, but typing it with no preceding PDF/print/DOM read is a shortcut signal. An agent that reports PRINT_2_PDF_8X11 as the answer has stopped one step early.

name: MapPanner
description:
Map Panner

Pan around the map to find the hidden treasure. Try searching in the southeast quadrant of the map, around coordinates (1400-1600, 1100-1300)...
notes: routes.ts: "Pan around a mysterious map to find the hidden treasure" (no variant field, i.e. the default). A 2000x2000 map (grid with text labels "x,y" every 200 map px) fills an overflow:hidden full-viewport surface; dragging (mousedown, mousemove, mouseup) translates it. No wheel, scroll or keyboard support. Completes when the viewport centre (innerWidth/2, innerHeight/2) is within 150 map px of (1500,1200). At 1280x900 that needs a total pan of about (-860, -750), more than fits in one drag below the fixed instruction panel (x 16-1112, y 16-112 at 1280 wide); moving the pointer onto that panel or out of the window ends the drag, so it takes at least two drags. The proximity check runs inside mousemove against the position from the previous render: a drag whose move is a single jump can land exactly on the spot without completing (verified); the next mousemove of any later drag completes it, and multi-step moves complete on the spot. Success: the panel text becomes "You found the treasure!" with "Password: CARTOGRAPHER2024" (plus a 💎 on the map). Viewport-dependent: the required pan distance depends on the window size.
mechanic: coordinate mouse drag (pan) on a plain surface

name: RightClickRevealHard
description:
Right Click Challenge (Hard)

This one is trickier! There are multiple areas. Only a specific small, hidden spot will reveal the true password when right-clicked. Don't get fooled by decoys!
notes: routes.ts: "Find and right-click a small, specific area among decoys." (HARD variant; the base right-click is in v1, this one adds the dialog and the tiny target). Three grey cards "Decoy 1", "Decoy 2", "Decoy 3". Right-clicking Decoy 1 or Decoy 3 opens a native alert("Nice try! But this isn't the spot. Keep looking!") that blocks the page until dismissed; a Playwright click that raises it does not return until a dialog handler dismisses it (verified: the solver hung until the handler was installed before the click). Decoy 2 itself has no handler. The target is a 32x32 half-transparent blue dot in the bottom-right corner of Decoy 2 with no text, only title="Right click me!" (Playwright AI snapshot, as in Playwright MCP / playwright-cli, lists it as generic "Right click me!" with a ref; the plain aria snapshot omits it). Right-click (contextmenu) on the dot shows "Password: HARD_CONTEXT_CONNOISSEUR" below the cards. A left click does nothing.
mechanic: native alert() dialog + tiny text-less target
